author: Associated Press
description:
Suspect Benny Caldera Jr held on bond as officials say they received ‘credible’ information about Austin threat

A 40-year-old man was arrested early Wednesday on suspicion of plotting to attack the Texas state capitol, authorities said.

The Texas department of public safety said in a statement that it received “credible information about an individual planning a violent attack” for Thursday in Austin.

Continue reading...
title: Man arrested over alleged plot to attack Texas state capitol

author: Patrick Barkham
description:
Simple deterrents can slash the number of razorbills and guillemots being trapped underwater, two-year study shows

Bird-shaped kites and a floating scarecrow are being tested to try to stop endangered seabirds drowning in fishing nets.

Every year an estimated 95,000 diving birds, including razorbills and guillemots, are accidentally caught in nets off European coasts.

Continue reading...
title: Floating scarecrows: how Cornish fishers are stopping seabirds drowning in their nets

author: Esther Addley
description:
Community-funded archaeological excavations of ‘really important’ sixth-century monastery also rewrite story of Lismore

To the residents of the Scottish island of Lismore, population 190, history is never very far away. The tiny island near Oban in Argyll has no row of shops or even a pub – if islanders want to meet for a coffee, the only place to do so is in the lively Gaelic heritage centre that records the many centuries of community life on the island.

This quiet place, documentary evidence records, was home to a monastic settlement in the sixth century AD, when missionaries from Ireland were first moving into northern Britain to spread Christianity. But apart from a few fragments of an early carved cross, there was almost nothing to see from this period of history.

Cont
title: ‘Hugely exciting’ finds on tiny Scottish island shed light on spread of Christianity

author: Nick Visser
description:
Follow the day’s news live.

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Shoebridge says people are sick of ‘messaging without substance’

David Shoebridge, the new Greens leader, says Australians are “sick of the messaging without substance”.

People are sick of the messaging without substance. What they’re asking for is they’re asking for a political party that’s going to go and fight for them and take on the 1% and take on the corporations. They want to see us fighting for that.

We have an incredibly united membership base. We have an incredibly united party across the country. And I expect that to be how we operate as a party room, how we operate as a leadership team and how we oper
title: Australia news live: ATO finds one-quarter of big firms pay zero tax; NDIS alternative Thriving Kids program begins

author: Shrai Popat in Washington and Ariana Baio in New York
description:
Pentagon head hails military with ‘no fatties, no trannies, no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps, no radicals’ in anti-DEI rant

  • Send us your questions about how the Iran war will affect US voters in the midterms

The US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, has confirmed plans to cut 20% of generals and admirals and declared “no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps” would be tolerated inside the country’s military.

Delivering his latest extraordinary attack on diversity, and dismissing reports of low morale within the US armed forces as “false claims”, Hegseth also suggested they were retaining service personnel at “record” rates.

Continue reading...
title: Hegseth confirms plan to cut 20% of US top military brass and rails at ‘beardos, weirdos and wimps’

author: Nick Robins-Early
description:
A year after his explosive tenure at Doge, the SpaceX CEO is back in the Trump administration’s good graces

Pete Hegseth announced on Wednesday that Elon Musk will co-lead a government project to study the future of warfare, marking the SpaceX CEO’s first return to government since he ran the chaotic, so -called “department of government efficiency”, or Doge. Musk will be joined by Palmer Luckey, CEO of the defense tech company Anduril, and Newt Gingrich, the former Republican speaker of the House.

A defense department press release on the effort, called Project Meridian, described its goal as “identifying the capabilities required to achieve absolute technological dominance on the next-generation battlefield”. The project will run for 120 days and culminate in an unclassified public report of its recommendations.
title: Pete Hegseth appoints Elon Musk to US taskforce on future of warfare

author: Associated Press
description:
No one was injured at Children’s World Early Learning Center and parents will appear in court, police said

The parents of a Detroit-area toddler who pulled a loaded pistol out of his backpack at a daycare will face charges in the case, police said on Wednesday.

In a statement, police in Canton Township said the parents would make an initial court appearance on Thursday. The Wayne county prosecutor’s office declined to offer details or additional comment, saying it would wait until a judge signs off on the charges.

Continue reading...
title: Parents of toddler who had loaded pistol in bag at Detroit daycare to face charges

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Democrats block measure they say didn’t go far enough – and was bundled with ‘poison pill’ voter ID rules

The US Senate on Wednesday blocked a Republican bill restricting stock trading by members of Congress, after Democrats refused to advance a measure they said would let lawmakers keep their portfolios and was bundled with voter ID rules they called a “poison pill”.

The 53-47 vote fell seven short of the 60 needed to open debate on the Stop Insider Trading Act, which the Republican-controlled House passed in July. Every Democrat and independent voted no, and the failure comes five weeks before the 3 November midterms.

Continue reading...
title: Senate blocks Republican bill restricting stock trades by US Congress members

author: Associated Press
description:
Shili Chen and Shouyong Zhang, both 77, charged days before Jonathan McKinsey and wife were set for hearing in divorce case

A California couple have been charged with murder after authorities say they shot their son-in-law to death Saturday in a public park, days before he and the couple’s daughter were set for a hearing in a bitter divorce case.

Shili Chen and Shouyong Zhang, both 77, were due in court Wednesday for an arraignment on the charges. The Associated Press was not able to reach an attorney for the couple prior to the court appearance. Their daughter, Candice Jang, could not be reached, though she appeared virtually at Wednesday’s hearing.

Continue reading...
title: In-laws charged with murder of New York Times games engineer in California

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Measles outbreak in the state has now reached 39 counties, with 943 confirmed cases and 176 hospitalizations

Pennsylvania has reported its fifth measles-associated death of 2026 as the state’s ongoing outbreak climbs to 943 confirmed cases across 39 counties.

The Pennsylvania department of health said on Wednesday that an unvaccinated Lancaster county resident who tested positive for measles had died. Health officials did not release further information about the individual, citing privacy protections.

Continue reading...
title: Pennsylvania reports fifth measles-related death of the year amid outbreak

author: Ariana Baio
description:
The charges are senior officials’ latest attempt to heighten voter fraud concerns amid midterm election campaigning

  • US politics live – latest updates

The US Department of Justice indicted another 10 individuals on noncitizen voting related charges on Wednesday as Donald Trump’s administration continues to pursue allegations of voter fraud raised by the president.

In the sixth announcement of its kind this month, the attorney general, Todd Blanche, and homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, said 10 people in Minnesota were charged with making false claims about cit
title: Trump DoJ indicts 10 individuals on noncitizen voting related charges in Minnesota

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
Noem cites irreconcilable differences in filing that comes after husband Bryon Noem involved in tabloid scandal

Kristi Noem, who was fired by Donald Trump after a rumbustious stint as homeland security secretary, is divorcing her husband, Bryon Noem, after 34 years of marriage, citing “irreconcilable differences”.

The divorce claim “for settlement purposes only” was disclosed in court records filed in Hamlin county, South Dakota, the state of which Noem was previously governor.

Continue reading...
title: Kristi Noem, former Trump homeland security chief, files for divorce

author: Alba Asenjo Domínguez
description:
No new indictments from eight-year investigation as state attorney general says church knew about abuse

More than 270 Catholic clerics sexually abused nearly 1,000 children across three Massachusetts dioceses over several decades, according to a report released by the state’s attorney general’s office on Wednesday.

The eight-year-long investigation did not result in new indictments, the office said, claiming that some conduct identified was not a crime under Massachusetts law at the time it occurred, and that in other cases the applicable statute of limitations had expired.

In the US, call or text the Childhelp abuse hotline on 800-422-4453 or visit their website for more resources and to report child abuse or DM for help. For adult survivors of child abuse, help is available at ascasupport.org. In the UK, the
title: Catholic clergy sexually abused nearly 1,000 Massachusetts children over decades, report finds

author: José Olivares in New York
description:
FBI accuses Chloe Freeman of federal misdemeanor in case of undocumented Mexican migrant arrested in Michigan

The federal government is charging a Michigan nurse accused of illegally helping an undocumented immigrant, who was being treated in a hospital, escape from immigration officials, court records unsealed this week show.

An FBI agent’s declaration submitted in a federal court accuses Chloe Renae Freeman, 33, of “instigating or assisting escape”, a federal misdemeanor, by helping a patient leave an Ann Arbor hospital while in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody in May. The patient, an undocumented immigrant from Mexico, had been arrested around two hours earlier by Customs and Border Protection (CBP) border patrol agents.

Continue reading...
title: Nurse charged with helping man in hospital escape from ICE custody

author: Kiran Stacey and Lisa O’Carroll
description:
Senior Downing Street officials reach out to thinktanks and pollsters as they look to test backing for reversing Brexit

Senior Downing Street officials have been reaching out to thinktanks and pollsters as they look to test public support for the UK rejoining the EU.

Aides to Andy Burnham have been talking to EU experts in a range of organisations about how the public would view a promise to rejoin, as momentum builds behind including such a pledge in the next Labour manifesto.

Continue reading...
title: No 10 gathering evidence on public support for UK rejoining EU

author: Alice Speri
description:
When one track failed, Trump administration rushed immigration case of Palestine rights advocate Salah Sarsour

An immigration judge has ruled that the president of Wisconsin’s largest mosque can be deported under a controversial, cold-war era law the Trump administration has sought to wield against foreign nationals who have been outspoken about Palestinian rights.

Salah Sarsour, a US permanent resident for nearly three decades, was detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement in March. He was released after a federal judge found he had probably been detained in retaliation of his advocacy for Palestinian rights, which t
title: US immigration judge allows cold war-era law to deport Wisconsin mosque’s president

author: Lauren Aratani in New York
description:
Trump criticized $2.4bn rehab amid attempts to pressure then Fed chair Jerome Powell into lowering interest rates

An internal watchdog said the Federal Reserve mismanaged costs associated with a $2.4bn renovation of its Washington DC headquarters, but noted that no criminal violations occurred, according to a report released on Wednesday.

For over a year, Donald Trump has centered his attacks against the Fed and former chair Jerome Powell around the renovations, including a months-long Department of Justice criminal investigation that was dropped in April.

Continue read
title: Federal Reserve watchdog finds no criminal violations for building renovation cost overruns

author: Oliver Holmes
description:
On morning service from Dubai to Tel Aviv, 150 passengers witnessed a horrific cockpit assault and a daring rescue

  • Pilot who stabbed co-pilot on Israel-bound plane may have tried to crash it, says Netanyahu

As flight FZ 1073 soared west over the waters of the Gulf towards Israel, its passengers may have bemoaned a 20-minute delay at takeoff. For a low-cost airline route, flydubai’s daily service to Tel Aviv is usually convenient and reliable. The nonstop flight takes about three and a half hours and departs early enough from Dubai that it usually lands at Ben Gurion airport at about 9am local time.

That was not the case for Wednesday’s catastrophic flight. The passenger jet never made it to its scheduled destination. Instead, it dropped thousands of feet in seconds before limping down to make an emergency landing in
title: ‘Whoever is hearing me, we need help’: how flight 1073 survived its 17,000ft plunge

author: Eve Livingston
description:
While the country’s screen sector is growing, only a fraction of production staff are Scottish themselves

Scotland’s striking Ardross Castle, the oldest star of Celebrity Traitors, which kicks off on Thursday night, is just one of the stops on the Scottish tourist board’s “screen tourism” trail.

From Outlander and The Odyssey filming in the Highlands and islands, to Glasgow city centre standing in for New York and Gotham City respectively in the latest instalments of Indiana Jones and Batman, film and TV is increasingly big business in Scotland.

Continue reading...
title: Crews filming in Scotland told to hire locals as industry booms

author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
description:
French president, speaking alongside Spanish counterpart Pedro Sánchez, says EU bid would be good news for UK and Europeans

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The French president, Emmanuel Macron, has reacted warmly to Andy Burnham’s suggestion that the UK could rejoin the EU.

“Welcome back,” the French leader said in English with a smile at a news conference in Madrid on Wednesday. Macron continued in French: “If the British want to come back and if the prime minister is moving in that direction, I think that is very good news, both for his country and for the Europeans.”

Continue reading...
title: Macron says ‘welcome back’ to Burnham suggestion UK could rejoin EU

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Donald Trump and six tech executives voluntarily signed the document, which included a misspelling, committing to safely developing AI

The White House misspelled “United States” under the signature of Donald Trump on an accord he signed with AI executives on Tuesday.

At the bottom of the accord on “Super Intelligence,” the term Trump has used to rebrand artificial intelligence, the president’s signature appeared as “President of the Unites States”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘President of the Unites States’: White House’s AI accord includes spelling error

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
PM also defends decision to release suspects on bail and expresses ‘complete confidence’ in security services

There are “strong indications” that Iran played a role in events in which five men were arrested near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire as part of a terror investigation, Andy Burnham has said.

Speaking to the media at the end of the Labour party conference in Liverpool, Burnham said he could not give any more details amid a police investigation, but that Iran was believed to be involved.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Strong indications’ that Iran played role in RAF Fairford incident, says Burnham

author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
description:
Seven others found guilty of lesser charges in connection to incident in 2021 when inflatable dinghy sank killing at least 27 people with four more missing, presumed dead

A Paris court has jailed six ⁠men for manslaughter over the deaths of at least 27 people in the worst mass drowning from a small-boat crossing in the Channel on record.

Seven other men were ⁠found guilty of lesser smuggling charges with varying degrees of seriousness, including facilitating illegal immigration as part of ⁠an organised gang and criminal conspiracy.

Continue reading...
title: French court jails six men for manslaughter over mass drowning in Channel

author: Guardian staff
description:
Late-night hosts weighed in on Trump’s relationship with tech leaders and the White House’s new AI-powered site

On Tuesday night, late-night hosts discussed a Maha summit in Washington DC, the White House’s new AI-powered website and Donald Trump once again falling asleep on live TV.

Continue reading...
title: Seth Meyers on Trump canceling $1bn in federal funds: ‘Is he adding a waterslide to the reflecting pool?’

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Traders see an about 35% chance of an October rate hike, down from ​about 45% following White House pressure

Good economic news boosted Wall Street’s main indexes on Wednesday, as a softer-than-anticipated inflation reading buoyed hopes that the Federal Reserve might not hike rates as soon ⁠as next month.

A commerce department report ⁠showed the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) ​price index stood at 3.4% on an annual basis in August against estimates of 3.7%, per economists polled by Reuters.

Continue reading...
title: Good news in US inflation report boosts chances Fed won’t hike rates

author: Jessica Elgot
description:
Prime minister’s pure political argument marks new era for party as he sets out his plans and priorities

The hottest ticket at Labour conference – after Andy Burnham’s speech – was an afterparty in Liverpool’s Baltic Triangle, headlined with a set by the noughties girlband Sugababes. As Labour activists and ministers belted out the lyrics under pink spotlights, it was hard not to draw some parallels with the party’s recent history.

There have been painful lineup changes and a lot of internal division, but this week onstage in Liverpool the originals are back together and they only played the hits. The fans can’t get enough.

Continue reading...
title: ‘He persuaded us’: Labour ministers moved by Andy Burnham’s emotional conference speech

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Unprecedented university donation from Citadel CEO Ken Griffin will go toward building a new Miami campus

Carnegie Mellon University will receive an unprecedented $3bn donation from the billionaire investor Ken Griffin, making it the largest single donation in the history of US education.

Griffin, 57, is the founder and CEO of Citadel, described as the most profitable hedge fund in history. The money is going toward a new Miami campus as well as big investments at the university’s longtime home in Pittsburgh.

Continue reading...
title: Hedge fund CEO gives $3bn to Carnegie Mellon University in historic donation

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Plane made emergency landing after pilot tried to crash aircraft, Israeli PM says, as officials investigate whether it was an attempted terror attack

One of the pilots of a plane flying from the UAE to Israel stabbed his co-pilot and appeared to try to crash the plane, the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, said, as Israeli officials said they were investigating whether the incident was an attempted terror attack on Israelis. Here is what we know so far:

A commercial plane travelling from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Israel was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, after an apparent brawl between its pilots prompted distress signals that briefly raised fears of an attempted hijacking. The flydubai flight was over Jordan when it diverted to Saudi Arabia, transmitting three eme
title: What we know so far about alleged stabbing of pilot by co-pilot on flight to Israel

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Cotality data shows median house prices fell in September as interest rates hit borrowing capacity

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Housing prices are falling in almost every suburb in Australia’s biggest cities, with values dropping faster in Brisbane than Sydney as the slowdown intensifies.

Prices nationally have fallen 5.2% from their peak in March to where they were a year ago, Cotality data released on Thursday shows.

Continue reading...
title: Brisbane and Sydney hit hardest by falling house prices as 5.2% shaved from Australian property values

author: Yvonne C Lam
description:
Two supermarket home brands claim equal first while the worst-ranked condiment has double the sugar content of almost all the other products

A condiment worthy of compliments, or one that gets a dressing down? Consumer advocacy group Choice has taste tested 29 store-bought mayonnaises, and found the cheapest product is also the best.

Aldi’s Colway Real Mayonnaise placed equal first with a score of 80%. A jar costs $2.79, or 61c per 100g – the lowest price per unit of the product spread. Judges relished its “mild” and “pleasant” aroma and “traditional mayonnaise appearance”, while noting its “creamy, smooth texture with balanced citrus acidity, subtle sweetness, mustard and whole-egg flavour”.

Sign up for a weekly email featuring our best reads
title: Australia’s cheapest mayonnaise is also the best tasting, Choice test finds

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Julian Hill says educational providers are being closely watched by government after course attracted non-genuine students

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Private colleges have issued nearly 3,000 last-minute enrolments to a diploma course that is being cancelled after allegedly being “misused” by non-genuine students, as Labor threatens to suspend providers that are manipulating new rules.

Guardian Australia revealed last month that private colleges were offering discounts to rush students into the graduate diploma of management (learning) ahead of
title: Australian colleges warned ‘do not try to game’ student visas after last-minute enrolments for cancelled diploma soar

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Senator Jim Justice of West Virginia criticizes immigration crackdown as ranchers’ associations condemn ICE activity

A close political ally of Donald Trump has broken from the administration’s aggressive immigration enforcement agenda and recommended it “step back” to evaluate what it could do better.

“To get better, the first thing you got to do is admit you’re doing something wrong,” Jim Justice, a Republican senator of West Virginia, told Politico. “And in this situation, with all that’s going on and all the stuff, we probably got to step back from it and say: ‘Maybe we’re doing something wrong here or there,’ and then adjust to that.”

Continue reading...
title: Republican urges Trump administration to ‘step back’ and rethink immigration agenda

author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
description:
Exclusive: Campaign comes amid backlash against tech company’s involvement with Israeli military and Trump’s ICE crackdown

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Tens of thousands of people have formally demanded NHS England blocks the Palantir-powered national medical data platform from handling their personal information.

More than 44,000 people have filed legal objections to their health data being shared with, stored in or used by the nationwide Federated Data Platform (FDP) operated using the US company’s AI technology.

Continue reading...
title: More than 44,000 file legal objections to Palantir NHS platform handling their data

author: Ashifa Kassam in Madrid
description:
As soaring rents and house prices across Europe​ feed into the political discourse, campaigners believe they have a rare opportunity to force housing to the top of the agenda

  • Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

It was billed as one of the largest real-estate events in Europe, attracting as many as 15,000 people ranging from investment firms to developers. But as the District trade show and summit got under way last week in Madrid, housing campaigners from 140 organisations across the globe turned up, intent on holding their own “counter-summit” to push back against the idea of housing as a financial asset.

Many of the campaigners arrived in the Spanish capital as Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman who uses a wheelchair
title: How Europe’s housing crisis is fuelling a new movement

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Corporation says story did not meet editorial standards after it attracts criticism from US and UK media

A BBC article that included a claim that a trend for bare nails was linked to “white supremacist standards of beauty” has been permanently removed from its website, after editors concluded it did not meet the corporation’s editorial standards.

The article, which first ran on the BBC’s website on 27 September, examined an apparent “viral craze” for bare rather than decorated nails. It said the trend had been flooding social media and fashion catwalks.

Continue reading...
title: BBC removes article linking bare nails trend to ‘white supremacist standards of beauty’

author: Alba Asenjo Domínguez in Washington
description:
Announcement comes two years after withdrawal was agreed to and 12 years since US mission to fight IS began

The Pentagon announced on Wednesday that it has formally completed its withdrawal of US troops from Iraq, two years after the withdrawal was agreed to and 12 years since the US mission to fight the Islamic State started.

After the announcement, Iran and its allies celebrated the departure as a victory, while Iraqi security experts worry that the withdrawal could give the Islamic State and others a chance to recover.

Continue reading...
title: Pentagon says it has formally completed withdrawal of US troops from Iraq

author: Geraldine McKelvie
description:
National inquiry will conduct local investigations and look at wider picture of sexual abuse and exploitation of children

Birmingham and Wales will be investigated as part of an independent inquiry into grooming gangs, it was announced on Wednesday.

The inquiry, chaired by the former children’s commissioner Anne Longfield, will have the power to compel witnesses and obtain documents to interrogate what individuals and agencies “did or did not do to protect children from being sexually abused”.

In the UK, the NSPCC offers support to children on 0800 1111, and adults concerned about a child on 0808 800 5000. The National Association for People Abused in Childhood (Napac) offers support for adult survivors on 0808 801 0331. In the US, call or text the Childhelp abuse hotline on 800-422-4453. In Australia, children, young adults, parents and
title: Grooming gangs inquiry to investigate offending in Wales and Birmingham

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
State governor and supreme court earlier refused calls for clemency for Christa Pike, who was convicted of murder

Tennessee’s first execution of a woman in 200 years was halted by a court on Wednesday morning an hour before it was set to take place.

The state governor and the supreme court had earlier refused calls for clemency in the case of Christa Pike, who was convicted of murder 30 years ago.

Continue reading...
title: Tennessee halts plan to execute woman for first time in 200 years

author: Phillip Inman
description:
Boost for John Healey before budget as GDP figure shows UK economy grew faster than first estimated in second quarter

  • Business live – latest updates

UK household income grew at a stronger pace than previously estimated during the first six months of the year, according to revisions of official data.

The rise in income per head to 1.1% between January and June followed an increase in the level of economic growth that illustrated the resilience of the UK economy since the outbreak of hostilities in the Middle East more than seven months ago.

Continue reading...
title: UK income growth revised upwards as markets hail ‘resilient’ economy

author: Andrew Gumbel in Los Angeles
description:
Steve Hilton’s long-shot campaign for governor is courting Golden state voters with unapologetically populist message

Steve Hilton stands almost no chance of becoming California’s next governor, but that isn’t stopping him from campaigning as though he was just one step away from pulling off the impossible.

The former Downing Street political adviser and Fox News host refuses to be daunted by the rancid political environment for Republican candidates this year, or by opinion polls that tell him he is lagging 20 percentage points or more behind his Democratic rival, Xavier Becerra.
title: ‘Of course I’m the underdog’: the British former spin doctor trying to turn California red

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
‘The era of writing blank checks to international bureaucracies is over,’ state department spokesperson says

Donald Trump’s administration has withdrawn the United States from the Council of Europe’s anti-corruption monitoring body, arguing that paying to belong to the multilateral group no longer serves US interests.

The US formally notified the Strasbourg-based organization on Monday that it was leaving the Group of States against Corruption, known as Greco – the latest step in a broader effort by the administration to pull back from international bodies it regards as inefficient, overreaching, or out of step with its priorities.

Continue reading...
title: Trump administration withdraws US from Greco anti-corruption monitoring body

author: Matthew Taylor
description:
Environment Agency warns residents of 6m properties to prepare for a wet and windy three months ahead

More than two million people in England are unaware their properties are at risk of flooding, as the UK braces for a wet and stormy start to the winter, according to the Environment Agency.

Experts say the next three months are more likely than usual to be wet and windy – due to a combination of large-scale weather patterns and the “subtle” impact of a supercharged El Niño – increasing the risk of flooding.

Continue reading...
title: Homeowners in England urged to check flood risk: ‘A third of people don’t realise’

author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
description:
Institutions have for years turned to China for funding opportunities but national security concerns are mounting

  • MI5 issues spy alert to UK universities over Chinese front company stealing research

The security alert issued by MI5 regarding a Chinese state-owned conglomerate accused of conducting espionage in the UK reveals the extent to which British intelligence remains concerned about Beijing’s influence, and risks casting a shadow over UK-China cooperation at a time when the bilateral relationship is enjoying a revival.

The UK’s domestic security service on Wednesday warned researchers and academics to cease work with the China Academy of
title: MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities

author: Ben Quinn
description:
Met calls move ‘milestone’ moment that paves way for ‘very best possible evidence for charging decisions’

Police investigating the 2017 Grenfell Tower fire have handed over files of evidence relating to 20 companies and 54 individuals to prosecutors.

The Metropolitan police described the move as a “milestone” moment that paved the way for what it said would be “the very best possible evidence for charging decisions”.

Continue reading...
title: Grenfell fire police investigators hand files on 20 firms and 54 people to CPS

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
PM’s oratory at least as good as Blair’s, says Andrew Marr, while Mail asks who pays for Honest Andy’s ‘New Jerusalem’

  • UK politics live – latest updates

When assessing British political speeches, even many critics of the New Labour years measure success against Tony Blair, a leader whose podium appearances are regarded as the peak of oratory.

On that measure, Andrew Marr, the former BBC political editor and now the New Statesman’s chief political commentator, reached for the ultimate accolade. “Rather to my surprise, I have to report Andy Burnham is at least as good a platform speaker” as Blair, he said. “Perhaps better.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘Oozing everyman charm’: what the papers say about Andy Burnham’s speech

author: Tom Ambrose (now) and Taz Ali (earlier)
description:
Israeli media say incident, which raised fears of possible hijacking, stemmed from feud between plane’s two pilots

  • Full report: Israel-bound passenger plane makes emergency landing in Saudi Arabia

The FlyDubai flight FZ 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia this morning after transmitting emergency signals.

According to Israeli media, a fight had broken out between the plane’s two pilots. Passengers described one of the pilots being seriously injured in an alleged stabbing.

The Boeing 737 plane, which Israeli officials said had between 160 and 180 passengers on board, transmitted a general emergency signal about two and a half hours after departing from Dubai, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24.

It diverted to Saudi Arabia as it flew over Jordanian airspace
title: Israeli minister claims ‘terrorist’ wanted to crash plane after Israel-bound flight’s emergency landing – latest

author: Andrew Roth and Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Support for white Afrikaners, anti-communism and others reveals how US redefining what qualifies as human rights

With hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a massive $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign against Brazil’s supreme court, and programs that would reward ideological allies in Europe who protect “western civilisational norms”.

Critics have focused on 43 awards of a combined $176.9m that will bolster rightwing and conservative causes around the world while likely angering US allies over interference in internal politics. The Guardian has seen a sample of the controversial grants, which makes up most of the $205m in funding that Congress has appropriated for the entire human rights and democracy fund (HRDF).
title: Top Trump figures push to direct human rights funding to rightwing causes

author: Matthew Taylor
description:
Study says UK-based banks provided $8.3bn in coal financing in four years, with Barclays and HSBC leading rise

UK banks are Europe’s biggest financial backers of the global coal industry, providing billions of pounds in funding for the climate-wrecking fossil fuel in the past four years, according to a report.

The study found UK-based banks had provided $8.3bn (£6.2bn) in coal financing since Cop26 in Glasgow in 2021, when global leaders pledged to “phase down” coal use. This compared with $4.9bn from German banks and $3.4bn from French banks over the same period.

Continue reading...
title: UK banks are Europe’s biggest coal financiers, report finds

author: Martin Belam
description:
Trump administration can deport immigrants to countries other than their homeland. Plus, 550lb bear returns to LA neighborhood

Good morning. The supreme court has ruled the Trump administration can resume deporting immigrants to “third countries”, or countries other than their homeland, without giving them any opportunity to contest their removals.

The six-justice conservative majority of the high court temporarily lifted a decision by a lower court that required the administration to provide immigrants sufficient notice and the opportunity to claim fear of torture or persecution in the countries where they were being sent.

What has the administration asked the supreme court to rule on about trans prisoners? The administration asked the justices to
title: ‘Third country’ deportation can resume, US supreme court rules | First Thing

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
Andrew Bailey’s comments come as fears grow that rogue models could take financial system hostage

  • Business live – latest updates

The governor of the Bank of England has said authorities must retain the “right to intervene” in the AI industry amid growing fears that rogue models could take the financial system hostage.

Andrew Bailey said the risks posed by the rapid advancement of frontier AI models – a number of which have gone rogue in recent months – were “real and increasingly significant” and reduced the ability of society to supervise and intervene when things went wrong.
title: We need ‘right to intervene’ in AI amid growing threat, says Bank of England boss

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
description:
Deal aimed at deterring small boat arrivals set to end as talks stall over French demand for EU-wide scheme

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The UK government’s “one in one out” deal with France, which was supposed to help deter small boat arrivals, is expected to expire on Thursday, government sources have said.

It is understood that negotiations have stalled over French demands for a Europe-wide deal instead, and a reluctance to scale up the numbers of people exchanged between the two countries.

Continue reading...
title: UK-France ‘one in one out’ deal to expire on Thursday, say sources

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
White House has labeled ads ‘public service announcements’ and has responded defiantly to criticism

Federal regulators have been urged to stop the broadcast of White House advertisements promoting Donald Trump that critics say amounts to government propaganda and violate laws against using public money to promote partisan causes.

Public Citizen, an advocacy group, called on the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to intervene and block further airing of three ads it said were “designed to boost the image and character of Donald Trump” as part of the Republicans’ campaign for November’s midterm elections.

Continue reading...
title: Trump campaign ads paid with public money violate federal law, critics say

author: Associated Press in Tel Aviv
description:
Israeli media say incident, which raised fears of possible hijacking, stemmed from feud between plane’s two pilots

A commercial plane travelling from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Israel has been forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, briefly raising concerns about a possible hijacking and prompting Israel to scramble warplanes.

Israeli media, citing security officials, said the incident on Wednesday stemmed from a feud between the plane’s two pilots, and everyone onboard was safe. The plane landed in Tabuk, a civilian and military base in the kingdom.

Continue reading...
title: Israel-bound passenger plane makes emergency landing in Saudi Arabia

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Kimya Holmes’ lawsuit over a news segment on a real-estate transaction invokes law that no longer exists

A New Orleans state court judge filed a police complaint against a local CBS affiliate after it aired a segment scrutinizing a real-estate transaction in which she was involved, with the jurist invoking a section of law that no longer carries criminal penalties, according to the journalist who reported the story.

The situation centering on New Orleans criminal court judge Kimya Holmes and investigative reporter David Hammer was only the latest in a series of high-profile matters pitting Louisiana journalists against members of the state’s court system.

Continue reading...
title: New Orleans judge files criminal case against CBS affiliate over reporting

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Bakery chain, whose sales are up 7.7%, says move is necessary to provide growth in ‘most cost-efficient manner’

  • Business live – latest updates

Greggs has announced plans to close four of its factories, in a move that could result in 740 job losses over the next two and a half years.

The bakery chain said it was consulting on the closures, which would initially cost £60m when including disruption costs and redundancy payments but then could create £20m of savings each year by 2028.

Continue reading...
title: Greggs announces plans to shut four UK factories that could cost 740 jobs

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Ex-Asda boss Andy Bond linked to plan, with buyout team understood to be negotiating with financial backer

Poundland’s management team are in “advanced talks” to lead a rescue bid for the ailing cut-price retailer that could save more than 11,000 jobs.

The former Asda boss Andy Bond, who ran Poundland for a number of years from 2016 then stepped up to its former parent Pepco before leaving in 2025, is understood to be part of the negotiations to take on the business.

Continue reading...
title: Poundland management in rescue talks that could save 11,000 jobs

author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
description:
Blast during search operation near border fuels political tensions amid attempts to revive diplomatic channels

South Korea has demanded an apology from North Korea over a landmine blast that injured three soldiers, saying they were hurt by North Korean mines on the southern side of the border.

Kang Hyun-woo, the director of operations at South Korea’s joint chiefs of staff, demanded an apology and “responsible measures” from Pyongyang over the blast, which occurred on 21 September during a search operation south of the border.

Continue reading...
title: South Korea calls for apology from North Korea after mine injures three soldiers

Kyiv mayor says debris had also been found at the site of a western embassy in the capital

Klitschko did not ​name the embassy, ⁠but said ​emergency services were ​heading ​to the ​site.

title: Russia targets communications and energy facilities in overnight drone attacks on Ukraine - Europe live

author: Aletha Adu Political correspondent
description:
PM says he is looking at all options and ministers will examine ‘what is doable’ and the ‘pros and cons’

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham has opened the door to the UK rejoining the EU, saying Britain could “go all the way”, as he prepares to reconsider Labour’s post-Brexit red lines.

The prime minister used a series of interviews after his emotional Labour conference speech to spell out how wide-ranging his consideration of Britain’s future with Brussels could be because Brexit had caused “more harm than good”.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham: UK could ‘go all the way’ by rejoining EU

title: David Shoebridge wants the Greens to ‘seize this moment’. Is his more combative style the answer?

author: Michael Goodier and Patrick Butler
description:
Councils collectively spent record 71.9% of core spending on adult and children’s care last year, analysis shows

Sixteen English councils spent more than 80% of their core funding on adult and children’s social care last year, highlighting the growing financial pressure on other local services.

Guardian analysis of government figures found that councils responsible for social care spent a net £42.8bn on adult and children’s services in 2025-26, equivalent to a record 71.9% of their combined core spending. Adult social care took 44.5% and children’s services accounted for 27.4%. In 2017-18, care costs made up 62.4% of councils’ core spending.

Continue reading...
title: Sixteen English councils spend more than 80% of core funding on social care

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
The prime minister says he wants to open a debate about the UK’s future relationship with Europe

Good morning. Andy Burnham’s speech is getting a mixed review in the papers, but there is general consensus that it is a consequential one – not one that we will have forgotten within a fortnight or so, but one that will make the next list of all-time important Labour conference speeches of the last 50 years.

If you are still catching up, here are three good places to start.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham says rejoining the EU among all ‘the options’ being considered – UK politics live

author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
description:
Cap poised to rise by 16% to equivalent of £1,999 for dual-fuel bill as impact of Iran war puts squeeze on homes

Household energy bills in Great Britain are predicted to soar by £276 a year for the typical household from January as the impact of the Middle East war continues through the coldest months of winter.

The government’s cap on energy prices is poised to jump by 16% to the equivalent of £1,999 for the average annual dual-fuel bill in a further blow to struggling households, according to figures from the leading forecaster Cornwall Insight.

Continue reading...
title: Energy bills in Great Britain forecast to jump by £276 a year from January

author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
description:
Exclusive: Environment secretary Angela Eagle to make pledge as part of efforts to protect against extreme weather

Half a million trees will be planted across England in the next three years to protect against extreme weather, the environment secretary, Angela Eagle, will pledge on Wednesday morning.

Mayors, local authorities, charities and grassroots groups will be given new funding and responsibilities for restoring natural landscapes such as wetlands, river edges and meadows, which can provide natural flood management and reduce the damage done by droughts.

Continue reading...
title: Half a million trees to be planted in England in three years, says government

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: ​At Labour conference members are basking in the glow of the Burnham bounce. But beneath the enthusiasm lies a growing sense that delivery must follow hopeful messaging

Good morning from Liverpool (and hello again to the newsletter subscribers I met in person, as I took First Edition on tour to Labour party conference).

It’s the first gathering of the party faithful since Andy Burnham ousted Keir Starmer in July, in what I’ve heard delicately referred to as a “soft coup”, and the theme of this conference is “Hope again.”

UK news | One of the five men arrested near RAF Fairford as part of a terror investigation that prompted fears of an Iran-backed plot called the police to report the incident. The call from the man, in his 20s and from London, was one reason armed police were scrambled to
title: Wednesday briefing: ​Can Andy Burnham live up to the party’s faith in him?

The New South Wales independent planner has approved the biggest coalmine project to ever go before it, allowing mining to continue until 2045 at a Hunter Valley project described by climate groups as a “carbon bomb”.

The Independent Planning Commission (IPC) has greenlit the Hunter Valley Operations (HVO) Continuation Project after a conten
title: Approval of biggest coal project in NSW planning commission’s history described as ‘infamous betrayal’

description:
Police allege Nicholas Scott killed 79-year-old then ‘set upon’ 59-year-old relative who arrived at Gurranang to sort out estate

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man accused of murdering two members of a family on the same property a fortnight apart has faced court.

The body of a 59-year-old man was found by police on Monday afternoon in a shed on a property at Gurranang, about 25km north of Grafton in northern New South Wales.
title: NSW man accused of murdering neighbour – and then murdering his relative two weeks later

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Culture secretary says UK will crack down further and be ‘pioneer of tech as a force for good’

Lisa Nandy has warned technology firms that the government’s online safety crackdown is not finished, saying that banning under-16s from social media platforms is only a “staging post”.

Earlier this year the government announced that teenagers under the age of 16 would be banned from accessing “high-risk” social media apps, while safer platforms would be subjected to restrictions.

Continue reading...
title: Nandy says children’s social media ban only ‘staging post’ in online safety drive

author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
description:
Relatives of Hollywood legend say her doppelganger could now be used for more glamorous roles

She shimmered in Hollywood’s silent movie era and lit up the first talkies – now Greta Garbo may be about to star in cinema’s new AI age.

More than a century after her screen debut and decades after her ashes were laid to rest in a Swedish woodland cemetery, the Hollywood superstar’s descendants are ready to consider an AI version of her taking a 21st-century film role.

Continue reading...
title: Reanimated AI Greta Garbo stars again … in a ball-bearing advert

author: Charlie Moloney
description:
Scheme will follow principles of Sure Start, helping families with infant feeding, mental health and bonding with babies

The government is rolling out a Healthy Babies programme to every local authority in England, as part of its efforts to expand a Sure Start-type system of help for deprived children and families.

It aims to support parents with infant feeding, their mental health and building strong bonds with their babies, alongside health visits, midwifery care and wider services.

Continue reading...
title: Healthy Babies programme to be expanded across England

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Jim Chalmers says ‘higher global oil prices flowing through to oil prices in Australia’ are to blame for inflation rising from 3.5%

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Inflation has jumped to 4% in the year to August, from 3.5%, as Jim Chalmers was again forced to defend Labor’s economic management amid fears the Reserve Bank will need to hike interest rates again before Christmas.

The increa
title: Inflation leaps to 4% stoking fears of fifth interest rate hike before Christmas

author: Kat Wong
description:
Former police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in early 2024

author: Pjotr Sauer in Kyiv
description:
Figure cited by minister highlights trade-offs Kyiv faces as it tries to keep normal life moving amid Russian strikes

Missile alerts are costing Ukraine an estimated $45m (£34m) for every hour they bring business to a halt, according to the country’s economy minister, as Kyiv searches for ways to keep the economy running under an intensifying Russian bombardment.

Russia has increasingly targeted the infrastructure underpinning Ukraine’s economy, striking industrial sites, warehouses, logistics hubs and datacentres in what Oleksandr Kravchenko, the minister for economy and the environment, described as an effort to “destroy pretty much the entire economy”.

Continue reading...
title: Missile alerts cost Ukraine $45m for every hour they halt businesses

author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
description:
National Trust says latest figures encouraging – with numbers of birds on the rise – but work still to be done

England’s most important tern colonies are showing signs of recovery after being hit by years of bird flu, flooding and increasingly unpredictable weather, new figures from the National Trust reveal.

The trust reported record numbers of little terns at Long Nanny in Northumberland, one of the UK’s most important breeding sites for what is the country’s second-rarest breeding seabird.

Continue reading...
title: Tern turnaround: colonies in England show signs of recovery after decline

author: Steven Morris
description:
Exeter museum to host DJ’s ‘collaboration’ with woodland fungi and artist’s map of her own body’s mycobiome

For one of the installations, a musician spent hours in woodland “collaborating” with fungi to create a soundscape inspired by the electricity they emit.

Another is a kinetic sculpture of an extinct fungus that honours Beatrix Potter not for her tales of mischievous rabbits but for her lesser-known skills as a mycologist – a fungi expert.

Continue reading...
title: Can a mushroom make music? Devon exhibition explores ‘cultural world’ of fungi

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Australian Transport Safety Bureau investigating staffing gaps as key factor in four incidents in July and August

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Modelling by Sydney airport’s air traffic control operators predicted elevated fatigue risks for staff at the time of a series of major safety incidents, with a review identifying runway incursions and near misses at 20% abov
title: Concern over Sydney airport as near misses and runway incursions at 20% above national average

author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
description:
The 74-year-old says he is leaving to spend more time with his family, including his six grandchildren

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Sign up for Guardian Australia’s free weekly media newsletter here

Financial journalist Alan Kohler, a familiar face on the ABC’s 7pm news bulletin, will retire in December after three decades as the public broadcaster’s highly respected financial guru.

Now 74, Kohler has been presenting finance, complete with idiosyncratic graphs, on the ABC for almost a quarter of a century, signing off each evening since 2002 with the catchphrase: “And that’s finance”.
title: ABC finance journalist Alan Kohler to retire after three decades as Jim Chalmers says he will be ‘really missed’

author: Abené Clayton
description:
Group of officers known as ‘riders’ in 2000s prompted longest arrangement of its kind in US history

After 23 years, a district judge has released the Oakland police department (OPD) from federal oversight, marking the end of the longest arrangement of this kind in US history.

In the early 2000s, a group of police officers known as the “riders” were exposed for offenses like planting evidence, falsifying reports and using excessive force against primarily young Black men. These actions led victims to file more than 100 civil lawsuits against the department. In 2003, as a part of the settlement of these cases, OPD was put on a federal court-ordered reform program.

Continue reading...
title: Judge ends federal oversight of Oakland police department after 23 years

author: Donna Lu Assistant editor, climate, environment and science
description:
A record 157,957 new EVs were sold nationally between January and June, according to the Electric Vehicle Council

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australians are buying electric vehicles at record levels, with sales more than doubling year on year and occurring at a rate equivalent to one EV sold every 100 seconds.

A record 157,957 EV sales occurred between January and June – an 117% increase on the same period last year, according to a new report released by the Electric Vehicle Council.
title: An EV sold every 100 seconds: Australian demand for electric cars more than doubles

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Nine American citizens have been killed by Israeli settlers or security forces in occupied West Bank since 2022

The US Senate on Tuesday evening rejected along mostly party lines a Democratic resolution that would have forced the state department to report to Congress on violence in the occupied West Bank, including the killings of nine American citizens by Israeli settlers or security forces over the last few years.

The resolution, led by the Maryland Democrat Chris Van Hollen, would have given the state department 30 days to report to Congress on those deaths and on wider human rights conditions in the territory, including Israel’s detention of Palestinian children.

Continue reading...
title: US Senate blocks resolution demanding accountability over Israeli violence in West Bank

description:
Shoebridge to stand on a joint ticket with Steph Hodgins-May – a first-term senator from Victoria

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

New South Wales senator David Shoebridge has joined the race to become the Greens’ new leader, with an increasingly crowded field revealing splits among the 11-member party room.

Shoebridge said on Wednesday morning he would stand on a joint ticket
title: David Shoebridge launches leadership bid ahead of Greens ballot at party retreat
